flagged.evidence: Step 2.1 uses [F1] to decompose $(s,r)$ in the basis $((q_n,p_n),(q_{n-1},p_{n-1}))$ for the theorem’s arbitrary index $n$. But the cited dependency [[cor-continued-fraction-convergents-are-reduced]] states only that for each $n\ge 0$ the vectors $(q_n,p_n)$ and $(q_{n+1},p_{n+1})$ form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $\mathbb Z^2$. That licenses the previous-pair basis only after shifting indices, hence only for $n\ge 1$. The present proof gives no separate justification for the $n=0$ case, where the needed pair is $(q_0,p_0),(q_{-1},p_{-1})=(1,a_0),(0,1)$.
